pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

DMTools CLI Wrapper

Usage:
  dmtools list                           # List available MCP tools
  dmtools doctor                         # Check current directory configuration
  dmtools run <json-file>                # Execute job with JSON config file
  dmtools run <job-name> [--key value]   # Execute a registered job without a config file
  dmtools run <json-file> <encoded>      # Execute job with file + encoded overrides
  dmtools <tool> [args...]              # Execute MCP tool with args
  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

DMTools CLI Wrapper

Usage:
  dmtools list                           # List available MCP tools
  dmtools doctor                         # Check current directory configuration
  dmtools run <json-file>                # Execute job with JSON config file
  dmtools run <job-name> [--key value]   # Execute a registered job without a config file
  dmtools run <json-file> <encoded>      # Execute job with file + encoded overrides
  dmtools <tool> [args...]              # Execute MCP tool with args
  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

Environment Variables:
  DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS    Comma-separated list of integrations (jira,confluence,figma)

  The tool automatically loads environment variables from dmtools.env
  (project root first, then the current working directory).

  Common variables:
  - JIRA_BASE_PATH, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN
  - CONFLUENCE_BASE_PATH, CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN
  - FIGMA_API_KEY
  - GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}

The app's taskTool — where is its executor? If the app's executor runs child runs, then inside a child run, `reply` resolves `currentSubagentId?.call()` = null (not wired!) → **reply is broken in app-hosted subagent runs?** That's pre-existing (the app never wired currentSubagentId). Not this PR's scope.

- More important for THIS PR: the app's `senderMailbox` closure reads `activeSubagentId()` — the ZONE. Does the app's child runs publish the zone? The zone is published by TaskExecutor.runSpawn/resumeChild — the same executor class. The app builds its own TaskExecutor? Let me check where the app's TaskExecutor is constructed and whether subagent runs go through TaskExecutor.runSpawn (yes — taskTool → TaskJobManager → executor). If so, zone works in the app.

- And `manager.mailboxOf(id)` — app's manager mailboxPrefix set at session init. OK.

But: the app never calls `wakeChildrenWithPendingMail()` (no inbox tick for children) and never wires wakeChild. So in the app, child reminders now land in the child inbox and stay. Documented tradeoff. I'll raise as IMPORTANT (ticket AC gap in the app host + mail becomes invisible vs before) — hmm, let me reconsider severity once more. The PR description (which I don't have — no pr_info!) — I only have the ticket. Ticket expectation #2: "schedule_message with default recipient from subagent X fires into X's inbox and wakes X." The PR implements fire-into-X for both hosts, wake-X only for CLI. The app gap is real but documented; flagging as IMPORTANT is fair ("should fix before merge or follow up immediately").

Wait, actually — I should double check whether the app has an inbox tick at all that could sweep children. The app's AgentService — `_wakeOnInboxMail` equivalent? The app drains MAIN's inbox on idle. Children: no. OK.

Now, the CLI wake flow subtlety I want to verify: **_assertResumable** — completed children resumable? Let me check quickly. Also check that resumeChild's early return for unknown handle throws StateError which the sweep's catchError handles → retirement. If a handle exists but status completed and sessionId is the placeholder '$parentSessionId/$id' (never attached — child never completed a session file)... _resumeSession(id, handle) opens the child JSONL by path — placeholder path won't exist → named error → resume throws → catchError → child retired. Wait — when is attachSession called? "at child completion when a session factory is wired". If the child COMPLETED, sessionId is real. If the child is `idle`... idle children (waiting for input) — do they have real session files? They ran, so presumably attached at completion of their run... "attachSession with the real JSONL path (at completion)". An idle child = a resumed child waiting? Either way, wakeable statuses (completed/idle) imply the child ran → session file exists. Failed children aren't wakeable. OK, reasonable.

One more wake-flow race: the sweep calls `wakeChild` = `_taskConfig.executor.resumeChild(id, childInboxWakePrompt)` DIRECTLY — not the manager's task_send warm-wake path. resumeChild enqueues the wake prompt INTO the child's inbox (`enqueueMessage` from selfId 'main', capText false), then drains ALL inbox (wake prompt + the pending reminder + any sibling mail), and prompts with all of it. Good — that's the "warm wake drains the inbox first" claim. Verified.

Now — **capacity/semaphore**: resumeChild acquires the semaphore. The sweep can start MANY wakes at once (one per child with pending mail) — each acquires a semaphore slot (Semaphore(4) default? CLI config). If 10 monitors' reminders fire simultaneously, 4 run, 6 queue on the semaphore — fine, they're unawaited background. But `resumeChild` adds `_resumesInFlight` + `_inFlightCancels` BEFORE semaphore acquire — so task_cancel works. And the sweep's `_wakingChildren` prevents re-stack. OK.

**Duplicate-resume guard via _assertResumable**: if the user concurrently does task_resume on the same child the sweep is waking: `resumeChild` checks `_resumesInFlight.contains(id)` (line 270) — rejects. Good.

Now check `_assertResumable` accepts completed.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

I've now read the entire diff. Let me summarize the changes:

1. **`lib/src/task/subagent_scope.dart`** (NEW) — zone-based identity: `activeSubagentId()`, `runWithSubagentScope()`.

7. **`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`** — `_childSenderMailbox()` helper.
8. **`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`** — wires senderMailbox from activeSubagentId() + manager.mailboxOf.

13. **test/task/subagent_identity_test.dart** (NEW) — 578 lines of tests.

Now let me review deeply. Key areas to scrutinize:

### A. `_deliveryTarget` logic in scheduled_messages.dart

```dart
String? _deliveryTarget(Map<String, dynamic> record) {
    final recordedTo = record['to'] as String? ?? _self();
    final from = record['from'] as String? ?? recordedTo;
    if (recordedTo != from) return recordedTo;
    if (!_owns(record['owner'] as String? ?? '')) return null;
    final owner = _ownerPrefix?.call() ?? '';
    final self = _self();
    if (owner.isNotEmpty &&
        recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/') &&
        recordedTo != self) {
      return recordedTo;
    }
    return (self != 'self' && self.isNotEmpty) ? self : recordedTo;
}
```

Considerations:
- `recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/')` — what if the record's `to` is a foreign-machine address like `name@machine`? Wait — `machine` addresses use `name@machine` format, no `/`. A subagent mailbox is `<prefix>/<childId>`. So `startsWith('$owner/')` is a reasonable guard.
- But what about the case where `recordedTo` names a subagent mailbox from ANOTHER session with the same owner prefix? The owner check `!_owns(record['owner'])` handles cross-session theft. Since the tool stamps owner = scheduler's session, a child-scheduled record has owner = parent session. OK.
- Potential issue: the subagent check happens AFTER `if (!_owns(...)) return null;` — fine.
- Edge: `recordedTo != self` — if owner prefix is `sid-1` and self is `sid-1/main`, a record addressed to `sid-1/main` explicitly would hit `recordedTo == self` and fall to legacy defaulting → delivers to self → same thing. OK.
- Edge: what if owner is empty AND recordedTo is `sid-1/child`? `owner.isNotEmpty` guard → falls to legacy default → re-addressed to self. Owner prefix is always set in hosts (session id). OK-ish.
- Edge: **what if a legacy record exists where `to == from == some-non-mailbox string`?** Not new.
- Hmm, one subtle issue: `_deliveryTarget` new branch returns `recordedTo` for any record whose `to` starts with `<owner>/` and != self — including a mailbox that does NOT correspond to any live subagent (e.g. child removed from handles, or a typo'd/foreign child id under the same prefix like `sid-1/foo` written by hand). The mail lands in an inbox nobody drains — same as before? Before the change, that record would be re-addressed to main, so main would see it (leak but visible). After the change it stays in the child mailbox. If the child is gone (session ended), the mail is stranded. This is the intended tradeoff (delivers as recorded), and wake sweep only covers live handles. Acceptable; maybe worth a suggestion about stranded mail for reaped children. Actually, does the CLI sweep pendingInboxCount for retained children only? `handles` = registered children of this session in this process. On restart, handles get rehydrated from registry records (rehydrate). The wakeChild = executor.resumeChild works via child session files. OK.

### B. `schedule_message_tool.dart`

```dart
final sender = senderMailbox?.call();
final id = await queue.schedule(
  text: text.trim(),
  delay: delay,
  to: (args['to'] as String?) ?? sender,
  from: sender,
);
```

Issues:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

Now let me review deeply. Key areas to scrutinize:

### A. `_deliveryTarget` logic in scheduled_messages.dart

```dart
String? _deliveryTarget(Map<String, dynamic> record) {
    final recordedTo = record['to'] as String? ?? _self();
    final from = record['from'] as String? ?? recordedTo;
    if (recordedTo != from) return recordedTo;
    if (!_owns(record['owner'] as String? ?? '')) return null;
    final owner = _ownerPrefix?.call() ?? '';
    final self = _self();
    if (owner.isNotEmpty &&
        recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/') &&
        recordedTo != self) {
      return recordedTo;
    }
    return (self != 'self' && self.isNotEmpty) ? self : recordedTo;
}
```

Considerations:
- `recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/')` — what if the record's `to` is a foreign-machine address like `name@machine`? Wait — `machine` addresses use `name@machine` format, no `/`. A subagent mailbox is `<prefix>/<childId>`. So `startsWith('$owner/')` is a reasonable guard.
- But what about the case where `recordedTo` names a subagent mailbox from ANOTHER session with the same owner prefix? The owner check `!_owns(record['owner'])` handles cross-session theft. Since the tool stamps owner = scheduler's session, a child-scheduled record has owner = parent session. OK.
- Potential issue: the subagent check happens AFTER `if (!_owns(...)) return null;` — fine.
- Edge: `recordedTo != self` — if owner prefix is `sid-1` and self is `sid-1/main`, a record addressed to `sid-1/main` explicitly would hit `recordedTo == self` and fall to legacy defaulting → delivers to self → same thing. OK.
- Edge: what if owner is empty AND recordedTo is `sid-1/child`? `owner.isNotEmpty` guard → falls to legacy default → re-addressed to self. Owner prefix is always set in hosts (session id). OK-ish.
- Edge: **what if a legacy record exists where `to == from == some-non-mailbox string`?** Not new.
- Hmm, one subtle issue: `_deliveryTarget` new branch returns `recordedTo` for any record whose `to` starts with `<owner>/` and != self — including a mailbox that does NOT correspond to any live subagent (e.g. child removed from handles, or a typo'd/foreign child id under the same prefix like `sid-1/foo` written by hand). The mail lands in an inbox nobody drains — same as before? Before the change, that record would be re-addressed to main, so main would see it (leak but visible). After the change it stays in the child mailbox. If the child is gone (session ended), the mail is stranded. This is the intended tradeoff (delivers as recorded), and wake sweep only covers live handles. Acceptable; maybe worth a suggestion about stranded mail for reaped children. Actually, does the CLI sweep pendingInboxCount for retained children only? `handles` = registered children of this session in this process. On restart, handles get rehydrated from registry records (rehydrate). The wakeChild = executor.resumeChild works via child session files. OK.

### B. `schedule_message_tool.dart`

```dart
final sender = senderMailbox?.call();
final id = await queue.schedule(
  text: text.trim(),
  delay: delay,
  to: (args['to'] as String?) ?? sender,
  from: sender,
);
```

Issues:
1. `from: sender` — when sender is null (main), `from` is null; queue.schedule likely defaults from to self. Need to check `queue.schedule` signature for nullability of `from`.
2. **`senderMailbox?.call()` is resolved synchronously per execution — fine. But what about the `to` address validation?** If a subagent explicitly passes `to: 'main'`, then `to='main'`, `from='sid-1/child'` → recordedTo != from → delivers to main. Good.
3. What if the tool args `to` is a non-String (e.g. the model passes a map)? `args['to'] as String?` — pre-existing cast; unchanged.
4. Doc comment says hosts wire `() => activeSubagentId() == null ? null : manager.mailboxOf(...)`. Fine.

Potential subtle bug: in the CLI/app wiring, `senderMailbox` returns `manager.mailboxOf(id)`. What if `mailboxOf` returns the raw id when no prefix? Let me check mailboxOf implementation.

### C. `task_executor.dart`

```dart
String? currentSubagentId() =>
    activeSubagentId() ??
    (_currentSubagentIds.isEmpty ? null : _currentSubagentIds.last);
```

The fallback to the stack head remains for "callers outside any scoped run". Under concurrency, that fallback is STILL wrong (that's the bug). When would a caller be outside the zone but still want identity? E.g. tools executed... hmm, actually all tool executions inside `_run` happen within the zone since `_run` is invoked inside `runWithSubagentScope`. Async chains preserve zones. But: **timer callbacks, microtasks scheduled OUTSIDE... no, closures capture the zone where they were created.** 

Wait, one real gap: `runZoned` propagates zone values to async callbacks created inside the zone. But what about code that runs on a NEW isolate? Tools run in the same isolate. What about `scheduleMicrotask` created outside? Fine.

BUT — a subtle one: `_run` internally may `await` futures; the zone persists through await within the same async function. Tool execution — is it invoked via a callback registered elsewhere (e.g., agent loop calls tool.execute inside its own zone)? The zone value lookup happens at call time via `Zone.current`, which for any code invoked (even synchronously) from within the zone body returns the zone — because synchronous calls from within zone code run in the same zone. Only explicitly-bound callbacks or new isolate/zone runs differ. Since agent.prompt(...) → loop → tool.execute all happen inside the zone, Zone.current is correct.

The fallback to stack head: keep for compat (e.g., tests or hosts that call tools outside runSpawn?). It's a documented fallback. The risk: some code path still hits the fallback under concurrency and gets the WRONG id silently — e.g., a tool executed from the main agent loop while children run in background: `activeSubagentId()` → null (main loop not in any zone) → falls back to stack head → returns the last-started child id! Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

No assignee — triage at will.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# gh-970: Inter-agent mail: subagent sender labels mixed up; self-scheduled messages land in main's inbox

## Description

## Symptom

In a session with several subagents (spawned via the `task` tool, background mode), inter-agent mail delivered to main's inbox arrives with **wrong sender mailbox labels** — the `from <session>/<name>` header names one subagent while the message content provably comes from another. Additionally, `schedule_message` calls that subagents target at *themselves* (recurrence pattern) are delivered to **main's** inbox instead.

## Observed instances (session 01a07bce-3250-7916-9472-419be50fb53f, 2026-09-26 ~10:00–10:35Z)

Subagents alive at the time: `dmd-monitor`, `fa-monitor`, `factory-flow-presentation`, `merge404-rca` (explore).

| # | Envelope sender label | Actual content (provable) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | fa-monitor baseline ("fa monitor baseline pass 1 …") — fa-monitor's own task-result confirms it wrote this |
| 2 | `.../factory-flow-presentation` | dmd-monitor first pass (dmd repo, PR #251/#249 state) |
| 3 | `.../fa-monitor` | dmd escalation about dmtools-dart PR #251 merge 404 — dmd-monitor's territory |
| 4 | `.../merge404-rca` | factory-flow-presentation's status report (archify validation stage, ETA) |

Plus: both monitors called `schedule_message` (delay 15m, default recipient = own mailbox). Both firings arrived as `from .../main: [scheduled] next monitoring pass` — in **main's** inbox, not the subagents'. The subagents never woke on their own; main had to relay the wake via `task_send`.

## Expected

1. `agent_message`/`reply` from subagent X is delivered with sender label X (or at least a stable, correct mailbox id).
2. `schedule_message` with default recipient from subagent X fires into **X's** inbox and wakes X.

## Impact

Orchestrator setups (one main + several monitoring/worker subagents) can't trust sender attribution — a monitor for repo A appears to report about repo B, and self-scheduled recurrence silently breaks (monitors stop waking; main must relay every tick).

## Notes

- The mislabeling looks like a swapped/shifted mailbox-name mapping in the session fabric, not agent confusion: each subagent's `task_observe` transcript and task-result show it produced the content that later arrived under a *different* subagent's label.
- Workaround used: main relays wake-ups via `task_send`; content is trusted over envelope labels.

### A. `_deliveryTarget` logic in scheduled_messages.dart

```dart
String? _deliveryTarget(Map<String, dynamic> record) {
    final recordedTo = record['to'] as String? ?? _self();
    final from = record['from'] as String? ?? recordedTo;
    if (recordedTo != from) return recordedTo;
    if (!_owns(record['owner'] as String? ?? '')) return null;
    final owner = _ownerPrefix?.call() ?? '';
    final self = _self();
    if (owner.isNotEmpty &&
        recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/') &&
        recordedTo != self) {
      return recordedTo;
    }
    return (self != 'self' && self.isNotEmpty) ? self : recordedTo;
}
```

Considerations:
- `recordedTo.startsWith('$owner/')` — what if the record's `to` is a foreign-machine address like `name@machine`? Wait — `machine` addresses use `name@machine` format, no `/`. A subagent mailbox is `<prefix>/<childId>`. So `startsWith('$owner/')` is a reasonable guard.
- But what about the case where `recordedTo` names a subagent mailbox from ANOTHER session with the same owner prefix? The owner check `!_owns(record['owner'])` handles cross-session theft. Since the tool stamps owner = scheduler's session, a child-scheduled record has owner = parent session. OK.
- Potential issue: the subagent check happens AFTER `if (!_owns(...)) return null;` — fine.
- Edge: `recordedTo != self` — if owner prefix is `sid-1` and self is `sid-1/main`, a record addressed to `sid-1/main` explicitly would hit `recordedTo == self` and fall to legacy defaulting → delivers to self → same thing. OK.
- Edge: what if owner is empty AND recordedTo is `sid-1/child`? `owner.isNotEmpty` guard → falls to legacy default → re-addressed to self. Owner prefix is always set in hosts (session id). OK-ish.

The mail lands in an inbox nobody drains — same as before? Before the change, that record would be re-addressed to main, so main would see it (leak but visible). After the change it stays in the child mailbox. If the child is gone (session ended), the mail is stranded. This is the intended tradeoff (delivers as recorded), and wake sweep only covers live handles. Acceptable; maybe worth a suggestion about stranded mail for reaped children. Actually, does the CLI sweep pendingInboxCount for retained children only? `handles` = registered children of this session in this process. ```

  `/tasks cancel <id>` routes by id; completions re-enter the parent
  as async-result messages (`agent://<id>` refs). Subagents are retained &
  addressable: real JSONL child sessions, `task_status`/`task_observe`/
  `task_send`/`task_cancel` (model-facing job abort), child-only `reply` +
  sibling `agent_message` (pending-queue + hop-capped),
  `completed_without_reply` notice. Child IDENTITY for tool calls is
  zone-scoped (`subagent_scope.dart`, gh-970): `runSpawn`/`resumeChild`
  publish the running child's id via `runWithSubagentScope`, and
  `TaskExecutor.currentSubagentId` reads the zone FIRST — the executor's
  in-flight id stack is shared by all concurrent children, so its head is
  "started last", not "executing" (that shift mislabeled every sender
  envelope and recorded replies on sibling handles). Hosts also resolve
  shared tools' self-mailbox semantics through the zone (`activeSubagentId`
  → `schedule_message`'s `senderMailbox`), and the CLI wires
  `SubagentManager.wakeChild` so mail that fires into a finished child's
  inbox (a self-scheduled reminder, sibling mail) resumes it in its own
  session — the child-side analog of the idle inbox wake (the sweep is

  per child per settle, a throwing wake retires the child).

  non-draining `hasPendingSteering` probe (external inbox, 2s poll).

  WITHOUT stopping the work — it continues as a background job and the user
  message is delivered at the step boundary. Tools ignoring the token keep
